title: PH Disasters 2026 Update — Aug 29, 2026
summary: OCD's August 29 report put the combined death toll from the habagat and cyclone sequence at 32, up from 31, with 19 injured and 3 missing plus 1 death pending confirmation; localities under a state of calamity grew to 117 (from 104) as 297 areas remained flooded, 281 of them in Central Luzon. In Lubao, Pampanga, an overflowing Sta. Rita Dam swept away a two-storey house on Aug 28, though residents evacuated safely. Combined infrastructure and agricultural damage reached ₱8.43 billion (₱6.11B + ₱2.32B), with ₱1.65 billion in government assistance disbursed so far, and the affected population rose to 8 million across 10 regions. Separately, the Visayas grid hit its 22nd red alert of 2026 on Aug 26 amid 32 forced power-plant outages, prompting the DOE to mandate NGCP install roughly 250MW of battery storage, while oil companies signaled a fuel price rollback (diesel -₱3.50 to -₱4/liter, gasoline -₱0.25 to -₱0.75/liter) for the week of Sept 1-2, reversing the prior two-week climb.

title: PH Disasters 2026 Update — Aug 28, 2026
summary: NDRRMC's August 27 report put the combined death toll from the habagat and cyclone sequence at 31, up from 29, with Benguet (15), CALABARZON (8) and Metro Manila (3) hardest hit; 19 remained injured and 3 missing. The number of localities under a state of calamity grew to 104, infrastructure damage reached ₱5.95 billion, agricultural losses hit ₱1.91 billion, and the affected population rose to 7.7 million people across 10 regions, even as evacuation-center numbers eased to roughly 28,000 as floodwaters receded in some areas. Fresh orange rainfall warnings hit Zambales and Bataan on Aug 27 evening as the southwest monsoon persisted. Separately, diesel and gasoline prices resumed climbing for a second straight week (diesel +₱2.31/liter, gasoline +₱1.08/liter effective Aug 25-31), reversing the prior retreat from March's crisis peak amid continued Strait of Hormuz-linked refinery disruption.

title: PH Disasters 2026 Update — Aug 25, 2026
summary: The number of local governments under a state of calamity from the habagat and cyclone sequence grew to 102 across 12 provinces and cities as of Aug 24, with Benguet becoming the latest to declare a province-wide calamity after cumulative landslide and flood damage topped ₱1.068 billion. The death toll held steady at 29 (19 injured, 3 missing) even as the affected population climbed to roughly 7.5 million people (2.2 million families) and infrastructure losses reached ₱5.1 billion. Typhoon Obet (international name Saudel), the season's 15th cyclone, briefly transited the Philippine Area of Responsibility on Aug 24 without making landfall before continuing toward Japan and China, but its track further enhanced the southwest monsoon, bringing renewed rain to Luzon into Aug 25. Separately, Philippine diesel and gasoline prices have retreated well below their March energy-crisis peak, though both ticked up slightly this week.

title: PH Disasters 2026 Update — Aug 21, 2026
summary: The habagat/typhoon death toll climbed to 29 (19 injured, 3 missing) as a newly formed Tropical Depression Neneng — the Philippines' 14th cyclone of 2026 — enhanced the southwest monsoon without making landfall. Over 6.5 million people are now affected, infrastructure damage reached ₱4.66 billion across 1,013 sites, and agricultural losses hit ₱1.73 billion. NDRRMC confirmed 88 cities and municipalities, including the entire provinces of Bataan, Bulacan, Pampanga and Cavite, are now under a state of calamity. President Marcos separately unveiled a plan for underground floodwater cisterns at 30 Metro Manila sites.
